    Parker impact score

    Source: R/inv-impact.R
    inv_parker_impact.Rd

    Computes the overall impact of an invader as the product of its range, its abundance (density or cover per unit area) and its per-capita or per-unit-biomass effect, I = R * A * E (Parker et al. 1999).

    Usage

    inv_parker_impact(.data, range, abundance, effect, .by = NULL)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per invader (or invader by region).

    range, abundance, effect

    <tidy-select> Numeric columns with range size, abundance and per-capita effect.

    .by

    <tidy-select> Optional grouping columns within which relative_impact and rank are computed.

    Value

    .data as a tibble with added columns impact, log10_impact, relative_impact (impact divided by the largest absolute impact within the group) and rank (1 is the largest absolute impact).

    References

    Parker, I. M., Simberloff, D., Lonsdale, W. M. et al. (1999). Impact: toward a framework for understanding the ecological effects of invaders. Biological Invasions, 1, 3-19. doi:10.1023/A:1010034312781

    Examples

    invaders <- data.frame(
  species = c("a", "b", "c"),
  range_km2 = c(1200, 300, 5000),
  density = c(4, 25, 0.5),
  effect = c(-0.02, -0.01, -0.3)
)
inv_parker_impact(invaders, range_km2, density, effect)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   species range_km2 density effect impact log10_impact relative_impact  rank
#>   <chr>       <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>        <dbl>           <dbl> <int>
#> 1 a            1200     4    -0.02    -96         1.98          -0.128     2
#> 2 b             300    25    -0.01    -75         1.88          -0.1       3
#> 3 c            5000     0.5  -0.3    -750         2.88          -1         1
